applicableAreas: All transformer pad locations on site (5 pads)
findings.comment: Transformer easements required for accessibility per UCM § 1.10.3 are not depicted on the site plan. Easement widths and locations must be shown to demonstrate adequate Austin Energy accessibility requirements around all five transformer pad installations.

Transformer pad dimensions matching Austin Energy Design-approved specifications for the specified service type (single-phase or three-phase) are not provided. Dimensions are not shown on the preliminary electrical design plan, and no Austin Energy Design detail sheets or approval documentation are included in the site plan submittal.

applicableAreas: Transformer Pad 4 in southeast quadrant near Building 7
findings.comment: Transformer Pad 4 is located only 0.6 feet from a parking or vehicle circulation area, placing it well within the 4-foot threshold that triggers bollard requirements. The electrical plan does not show 4-inch minimum diameter galvanized rigid metal posts (bollards) or reference to Austin Energy Design-approved equipment pad detail sheets specifying bollard placement and spacing.

applicableAreas: All transformer pad locations (if fences are adjacent)
findings.comment: Required clearances from fences and gates (5 feet for sides with operators/controls, 3 feet for sides without) cannot be verified. No fence locations are dimensioned relative to transformer pads, and access door orientations (which determine whether a side has operators/controls) are not indicated on the electrical plan.

Clearances of 3 feet to brick/masonry buildings require Austin Energy Design written approval documentation and verification that four conditions are met: (1) not in confined space, (2) 10+ feet to windows/doors/ducts, (3) 15+ feet vertical clearance to windows/doors/ducts, and (4) 3-hour fire rating. No such approval documentation, fire rating verification, or dimensional evidence is provided in the site plan.

Minimum 5-foot clearances from balconies, building overhangs, and protection from coverings/structures directly above pads cannot be verified. No architectural elevations or building cross-sections are provided showing these elements relative to transformer pad locations.

applicableAreas: All transformer pad locations (for oil-filled equipment)
findings.comment: Minimum 12-foot horizontal clearance from windows, doors, or ventilating ducts (when window/door/duct is less than 12 feet from grade or has less than 5 feet lateral separation) cannot be verified. The service type (single-phase vs. three-phase, oil-filled vs. dry-type) is not specified, and no floor plans showing windows/doors relative to transformer pads are provided.

Minimum 2-foot clearance from back of sidewalks cannot be verified. The electrical plan does not dimension distances from transformer pads to sidewalk/curb back-of-line, and it is unclear whether pads are properly positioned relative to this reference line.

Clearances from stairwells serving as fire exits cannot be verified. No stairwell locations are identified on the electrical plan or correlated with transformer pad locations. Building floor plans are not provided to verify this requirement.

Hot-stick use area minimum 10-foot clearance to open area or adjacent building/structure cannot be verified. The access door orientation and location are not indicated on the electrical plan, making it impossible to identify which side qualifies as the 'access door side' and measure clearances accordingly.

Minimum 15-foot clearance requirement for hot-stick use area when facing a confined space (niche, vault, or area enclosed on 3+ sides) cannot be verified. Access door orientation is not shown, and building configuration relative to each pad is not dimensioned to determine if any face a confined space.

applicableAreas: All transformer pad locations in relation to fire hydrant
findings.comment: Minimum 5-foot clearance from fire hydrants cannot be verified. While a private fire hydrant is shown on the fire protection plan (Sheet 10), the specific location is not dimensioned relative to transformer pad positions, and no clearance measurements are provided.

applicableAreas: All transformer pad locations and vicinity
findings.comment: Trees within 10 lateral feet of pad-mounted equipment or within 15 lateral feet of overhead distribution conductors must be identified as utility-compatible per ECM Appendix F. Tree species and locations relative to specific transformer pad locations are not verified; the landscape plan and tree list do not cross-reference trees to transformer pads or confirm utility-compatible species designations.

Minimum 10-foot lateral clearance from access door side and 5-foot clearance from other sides for shrubs and low-lying vegetation cannot be verified. Vegetation locations are not dimensioned relative to transformer pads, and access door orientations (which determine which side has the 10-foot requirement) are not indicated.

Root barriers (minimum 4 feet deep, installed 5 feet from equipment) are required for trees within 20 lateral feet of underground electric equipment. No trees are identified within 20 feet of transformer pad locations on the provided landscape documentation, and root barrier details are not shown for any trees relative to the pads.
Minimum 5-foot clearance from dumpsters cannot be verified. Dumpster locations are not identified or dimensioned relative to transformer pad positions on the site plan.
Minimum 5-foot clearance from bike racks cannot be verified. Bike rack locations relative to transformer pad positions are not shown or dimensioned on the site plan.
Minimum 5-foot clearance from light poles cannot be verified. Light pole locations are not correlated with transformer pad positions on the electrical or photometric plans.

Minimum 15-foot clearance from fire lanes cannot be verified. While fire zones and lanes are shown on the fire protection plan, specific distances from transformer pad locations to these restricted areas are not dimensioned.

Minimum 5-foot clearance between multiple transformer pads cannot be verified. While five transformer pads are shown on the electrical plan, no dimensions are provided indicating spacing between pads.

Minimum 12-inch horizontal and vertical clearance from other underground utilities (excluding gas, fuel, steam) cannot be verified. Utility routing and transformer pad locations are shown on separate sheets without dimensioned separations indicating compliance with the 12-inch requirement.

applicableAreas: All transformer pad locations and underground utility routing
findings.comment: Verification that transformer pads and underground facilities do not cross over or under other utility lines, and that customer buildings/foundations are not installed over Austin Energy underground facilities cannot be provided. Cross-sectional views showing vertical relationships are not included in the submittal.

Minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from overhead distribution line conductors cannot be verified. No overhead distribution lines or facilities are shown on the electrical plan, and no clearance dimensions are provided relative to proposed structures and vegetation.

Minimum 15-foot radius clearance from overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors (measured from conductors, not pole centerline) cannot be verified. No overhead distribution conductors are identified on the electrical plan, and no radius clearances are dimensioned.

Cross-section drawings demonstrating vertical clearances in access paths with overhead structures, parking garages, enclosed areas, or niches are not provided. Without these cross-sections, compliance with vertical clearance requirements cannot be verified.

applicableAreas: All transformer pad locations (if oil-filled equipment)
findings.comment: Grading plan drainage direction for oil-filled equipment (liquid flow must be away from buildings) cannot be verified. Transformer equipment type (oil-filled vs. dry-type) is not specified, and grading slopes around transformer pad locations are not shown on the grading plan.

Location of all transformer pads 100% on private property (not in public right-of-way or straddling property lines) cannot be fully verified. One pad was measured at 17.1 feet from property line, but the remaining four pad locations are not dimensioned relative to property boundaries on the electrical plan.

Verification that transformer pads are not located in prohibited easements (drainage, water, sewer, electrical easements under overhead lines) cannot be confirmed. While easements are shown on the site plan, specific dimensions showing transformer pad locations relative to easement boundaries are not provided.

Electrical routing from transformer to meter being 100% on private property cannot be verified. No dimensional evidence is provided showing that electrical conduit routing from each transformer pad to its associated meter is entirely on customer property and does not cross public right-of-way.
